newsitem.title: EGYPT: Land mine kills Nigerian on Egypt-Libya border.
newsitem.headline: Land mine kills Nigerian on Egypt-Libya border.

text.p: A Nigerian man stuck on the Libyan-Egyptian border since May last year was killed when he trod on a mine near a camp for stranded Palestinians, Egyptian security sources said on Wednesday.
Mamadou Tahiri, 38, had been staying in the camp in no man's land with about 200 Palestinians because neither the Libyan or Egyptian authorities will let him cross the border.
An aid worker who spent Monday night at the camp said Tahiri had been acting strangely in the evening, running around shouting "Allahu Akbar (God is Great)" and predicting his death.
There was a loud explosion around dawn and Tahiri had gone. Camp residents concluded that Tahiri had stepped on a mine.
The Egyptian security sources confirmed later they had found traces of Tahiri's body several hundred metres (yards) away.

In May last year Tahiri flew to Cairo airport and tried to enter Libya overland. The Libyans refused to let him in and the Egyptian authorities refused to let him back. He was one of several Africans in the same predicament.

U.N. agencies and other humanitarian organisations have been trying to find countries to take in the Palestinians, many of whom have been living in appalling conditions on the border for almost 18 months.
Libya threw them out as a political gesture of protest against Israeli-Palestinian peace agreements.
